adaptations.change: Convert the adapter env map to a string-only record and do not merge parent process values.
adaptations.reason: The library accepts a string record, while the adapter exposes a process env shape with optional undefined values.
The adapter spawner options do not carry cwd, and the default Bun spawner inherits the current working directory.

adaptations.change: Use killGraceMs when present, otherwise CLI_KILL_GRACE_MS at 250 ms.
adaptations.reason: The adapter default is mirrored so abort and timeout behavior stays aligned.

adaptations.change: Use a named WATCHDOG_BACKSTOP_MS value of 120000.
adaptations.reason: The adapter bounds normal runs with AbortSignal deadlines; the library still requires a backstop.

adaptations.change: Send the prompt only when promptOnStdin is true; otherwise use the library ignore sentinel.
adaptations.reason: This matches the adapter's prompt-on-stdin contract without adding parent input.

adaptations.change: Map numeric exit code first, then signal to 128 plus signal number, then -1.
adaptations.reason: The adapter journals signal termination as an exit_code-compatible number.

adaptations.change: Throw on the library spawn-error outcome.
adaptations.reason: The adapter maps a thrown spawn failure to the same spawn-failed shape as Bun.spawn.

adaptations.change: Use superviseProcess stdout/stderr callbacks as the only stream consumers and buffer stdout lines plus stderr bytes in memory.
adaptations.reason: The library puts child streams in flowing mode and resolves exit after stdio closes; adapter-paced iteration must not delay exit or lose early chunks. Buffering is eager and unbounded in this test shim.

divergences.note: The library signals the process group; the current default adapter signals the direct child. These parity cases observe only the exec child.

divergences.topic: Exit resolution after stdio versus leader exit
divergences.note: The library resolves exit after child stdio ends and the process group is gone, while the default resolves on leader exit. A lazy library stdout reader can delay exit, so the shim buffers through supervisor callbacks.
The library arm carries a watchdog backstop because the library API requires it; the adapter normally bounds runs through abort signals.
